newsitem.title: USA: US refiners look to Asia to quench thirst for oil.
newsitem.headline: US refiners look to Asia to quench thirst for oil.

text.p: In a rare market move, at least two U.S. refiners have looked to the Far East recently to quench their thirst for crude oil, traders said on Friday.
Privately held Koch Oil on July 9 sold a Malaysian combination cargo of 550,000 barrels of Tapis and 470,000 barrels of Labuan to Valero for delivery at the end of August.
The Tapis was placed at six cents over October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on a delivered basis, while the Labuan fetched parity to October WTI, traders said.
Separately, Swiss trader Vitol on July 10 sold an Indonesian Widuri cargo to a U.S. refiner for delivery around August 20 at about $1.35 under WTI, traders said.
Only an unusual combination of market conditions makes it economic to bring far-flung Asian crude to U.S. Gulf Coast.
"You need really steep contango in WTI and you need Southeast Asian prices to be weak," a trader for a major U.S. refiner said.
It takes about 35-36 days to transport crude from Asia to the Gulf Coast.
Tapis is a light sweet grade with an API gravity of 45.2 degrees and 0.03 percent sulfur. Labuan is 32.1 API with 0.07 percent sulfur.
Widuri is 33.2 API with 0.07 percent sulfur.
